update description: The Specify Needs phase now leverages end-to-end process automation and AI wherever possible. Activities such as gathering, synthesizing, and structuring stakeholder input, analysis of solution options, and drafting of business case materials are performed by automated and AI-powered processes. Staff—such as Junior Evaluation Officers—are expected to concentrate on higher-value work: interpretation, contextual analysis, prioritization, and oversight of outputs produced by automation.
impact reasoning: The role of the Junior Evaluation Officer will shift away from manually conducting routine literature and data synthesis, as well as initial documentation and drafting. Their responsibilities will increasingly include (a) reviewing, validating, and contextualizing outputs generated by automated and AI tools; (b) focusing on interpretation, stakeholder nuance, and the strategic alignment of identified needs; and (c) providing feedback and improvements to AI/automation workflows. Routine, repetitive collection and basic research tasks are reduced, but oversight, value-added analysis, and stakeholder engagement increase.

affected work-description elements.element: Key Activities: 'Undertakes assigned tasks related to specific elements of evaluation projects such as, conducting literature and data research, identifying, gathering, analyzing and synthesizing quantitative and qualitative data; participating in the conduct of interviews, and focus groups, applying analytical tools and techniques to determine implications of evaluation results and formulating conclusions.'
affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: This will shift from hands-on manual research and data synthesis to a more oversight-driven function: the officer will review and validate literature/data research carried out by automation, focus on identifying gaps/misclassifications in AI-produced outputs, and provide domain-specific interpretation for nuanced or context-sensitive cases. They will also need to understand the limitations and potential biases of automated outputs.

gaps.justification: As more literature review and data synthesis are automated, skill will be required to critically assess AI-generated content for accuracy, completeness, and bias.
gaps.name: AI Output Validation and Oversight
gaps.description: Ability to review, interpret, and verify the quality, completeness, and accuracy of AI/automation-generated literature reviews, summaries, and synthesized datasets; includes understanding limits of automation and recognizing potential algorithmic bias.

gaps.justification: Officers must now provide feedback and supervisorial guidance to AI system design or configuration, suggesting how outputs can be improved for policy relevance or analytic nuance.
gaps.name: Human-in-the-Loop Feedback Provision
gaps.description: Capacity to provide effective feedback or corrections to improve automated workflows, tune AI system outputs, and communicate contextual needs to technical teams.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: The focus will move from manual search/discovery and data mining to: (a) evaluating the relevance and accuracy of literature/data sources identified by AI systems; (b) determining the strategic value of results surfaced by automated systems; and (c) recommending fixes or further investigation when automated results are insufficient.

gaps.justification: Understanding and validating AI-driven data source selection or automated literature review requires digital and analytic literacy.
gaps.name: Digital and AI Literacy
gaps.description: Basic understanding of how automation and AI systems aggregate, synthesize, or select information; ability to spot errors, gaps, or biases in digital outputs and explain why certain sources/outputs are or are not relevant.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: Interpreting findings will increasingly include scrutinizing AI-generated summaries, recommending refinements to retrieval/analysis algorithms, and deciding which insights require deeper manual follow-up or contextual adjustment.

gaps.justification: To recommend method enhancements and interpret AI-driven outputs, officers will need a working knowledge of AI/automation methods in data retrieval and synthesis.

gaps.description: Awareness of the strengths, weaknesses, and suitable use cases for automated data retrieval and synthesis techniques—enabling evidence-based recommendations and risk identification.

affected work-description elements.element update reasoning: There will be an increasing emphasis on communicating how AI-driven findings were reached, explaining what was automated versus what required human intervention, and discussing any limitations or interpretive nuances in machine-generated outputs.

update description: AI and automation now continuously identify and synthesize requests, changes, and feedback relating to the need for new statistics. Their activities are less about 'raw' discovery and more about expert filtering, confirmation, and insight.
